### Automated Aviation Safety Issue Analysis App (South Korea, 2024-01-01)
Organisation: Aviation Safety Technology Institute (Republic of Korea), with National Information Society Agency
Layer: Government workflows, Compliance & supervision, Crisis response, Service design & UX
Type: Deployment
Summary: An AI-powered application that automates the processing and analysis of aviation safety data. Users input accident-related documents, and the system automatically translates, summarizes, classifies the accident type, and provides associated risk factors. The app also generates Excel files for secondary analysis and retrieves similar historical accident cases. It was developed to address inefficiencies in manual data processing by specialized analysts and support compliance with ICAO international standards for national aviation safety management.
Why it matters: The system represents a shift from manual data integration and analysis by specialized analysts to automated, end-to-end processing of unstructured aviation accident documents using generative AI. It combines document ingestion, multilingual translation, summarization, classification, and risk factor extraction in a single automated workflow. The system autonomously executes a multi-step analytical workflow upon document input: it 'automatically classifies the accident type' and 'provides associated risk factors' without human initiation of each step. The source states that inputting documents 'triggers translation and summarization' and that the app was developed to validate 'automation performance' for 'AI-based aviation safety data processing, safety issue identification, and document generation'.
What technology: Built using a large language model (LLM) fine-tuned on Q&A datasets derived from SKYbrary aviation accident articles, with an established aviation accident classification system and risk factor database. The system preprocesses data into LLM-understandable format and was optimized through continuous technical review.
Sources:
- Automated Analysis of Aviation Safety Issues: Hyper-Scale AI PoC — https://apolitical.co/en/navigator/case-studies/automated-analysis-of-aviation-safety-issues-hyper-scale-ai-poc

### Fire Access Route and Evacuation Route Guidance System (South Korea, 2024-01-01)
Organisation: National Information Society Agency (NIA), Republic of Korea
Layer: Crisis response, Government workflows
Type: Deployment
Summary: An AI and IoT-integrated system that analyzes real-time building data to calculate optimal evacuation routes for occupants and access routes for firefighters during fire incidents. It extends beyond traditional alarm notifications to provide dynamic, data-driven guidance for emergency response. Launched in 2024.
Why it matters: Moves beyond static alarm systems to real-time, adaptive route optimization that simultaneously serves both evacuees and emergency responders using live sensor data. The system autonomously analyzes real-time information and provides optimal routes without requiring human initiation of each calculation; it independently determines and delivers evacuation and access strategies based on live data analysis during active fire incidents.
What technology: Integrates AI with IoT sensors for real-time data collection and processing; specific models or platforms not stated.
Sources:
- Development of a Fire Access Route and Evacuation Route Guidance System based on the BDApp (Fire Remote Control Service) — https://apolitical.co/en/navigator/case-studies/development-of-a-fire-access-route-and-evacuation-route-guidance-system-based-on-the-bdapp-fire-remote-control-service

### Puerto Rico AI-powered Hiring Platform (United States, 2024)
Organisation: Government of Puerto Rico
Layer: Government workflows, People & culture
Type: Deployment
Summary: A standardized digital hiring platform launched in 2024 to unify recruitment across Puerto Rico's government agencies, replacing fragmented paper-based processes. It uses machine learning and natural-language processing to parse resumes, identify candidate skills, and match them to vacancy requirements while masking names to reduce bias.
Why it matters: It consolidates 56 separate agency-specific hiring systems into one platform that automatically screens and matches candidates by skills rather than keywords, and proactively suggests additional matching vacancies to applicants to broaden the talent pool. The AI autonomously handles the initial screening to shortlist candidates by skills without human intervention for each application, reading resumes and identifying skills to match against vacancy requirements. It also proactively shows applicants other open positions across government that fit their skills, stating that 'the AI handles the initial screening to shortlist candidates by skills' and 'shows the applicant other open positions across government that fit their skills'.
What technology: Built on Eightfold AI's talent intelligence platform, utilizing machine learning and natural-language processing to analyse unstructured text in resumes and applications for skills extraction and matching.
Sources:
- Puerto Rico's AI-powered hiring platform: Matching candidates to government jobs by skills — https://apolitical.co/en/navigator/case-studies/puerto-rico-s-ai-powered-hiring-platform-matching-candidates-to-government-jobs-by-skills

### Mobile Phone Detection Camera Program (Australia, 2023-03-30)
Organisation: Transport for NSW
Layer: Compliance & supervision
Type: Deployment
Summary: The Mobile Phone Detection Camera Program uses AI-powered fixed and transportable cameras across New South Wales to detect drivers illegally using mobile phones. The system captures images of passing vehicles in all traffic and weather conditions, uses artificial intelligence to automatically review images and detect potential offenses, and since 1 July 2024 has also enforced seatbelt non-compliance.
Why it matters: The system employs AI to autonomously review images in real-time, automatically excluding and permanently deleting images of non-offending drivers within an hour while routing potential offenses to human reviewers, representing a scalable automated enforcement mechanism that has expanded from phone use to seatbelt compliance. Artificial intelligence software automatically reviews images and detects potential offending drivers. It excludes images of non-offending drivers from further action. Images rejected by the artificial intelligence are permanently and irretrievably deleted, typically within an hour of detection.
What technology: The system uses multiple cameras and an infra-red flash to capture clear images of passing vehicles in all traffic and weather conditions. Artificial intelligence software automatically reviews the images to detect potential mobile phone and seatbelt offenses before human verification.
Sources:
- https://www.transport.nsw.gov.au/roadsafety/topics-tips/mobile-phones

### Online Cybersquat Hunter (OCH) (Singapore, 2023-03-05)
Organisation: Home Team Science and Technology Agency (HTX)
Layer: Cyber security
Type: Deployment
Summary: The OCH uses artificial intelligence with image and text analytics to scan two million sites daily, detecting fake websites that mimic government agencies or news organisations and facilitating their takedown. First deployed in late 2020 to protect Ministry of Home Affairs sites, it has been extended to other government organisations and identified over 10 fake news websites during a 2022 trial, contributing to the blocking of approximately 20,000 scam websites.
Why it matters: Autonomous daily scanning of millions of sites using combined image and text analytics to detect cybersquatting and visual impersonation, with automated takedown capabilities and extension to track resurrected scam sites through database matching. The OCH autonomously executes daily scans of two million sites and takes down detected fake ones without human initiation of each individual action, as described by its capability of 'picking up fake ones and taking them down'. Additionally, Synweb automatically checks sites against databases to identify resurrected scams, and the Scam-Site Indicator automatically predicts scam probability.
What technology: Utilises artificial intelligence with image and text analytics for detection, machine learning algorithms for scam prediction, and database matching capabilities for identifying resurrected sites with different domains.
Sources:
- Fake ST, Zaobao and CNA news sites that promote gambling detected and blocked — https://www.straitstimes.com/singapore/fake-st-zaobao-and-cna-news-sites-that-promote-gambling-detected-and-blocked
